primitives.note: Q, E and R each deal magic damage on cast (Q on a delay while the soldier dashes, E instantly on the dash, R after a short cast+travel delay); each is simply cast on cooldown for direct damage.
The summoned Sand Soldier substitutes for Azir's basic attack and deals the actual on-hit magic damage instance; Azir himself does not swing when a soldier is in range.

W is cast from a stock of up to 2 charges that Azir periodically regenerates (like Arise!'s Riot 'stock' mechanic), each charge costing mana plus one soldier use; this ammo/charge pool bounds how often soldiers can be replaced inside the fight.

The soldier's stab damage is modified by target state: a level-scaling percentage bonus for enemies hit beyond the closest in the line, and a flat 25% multiplier for a second/subsequent soldier attacking a target already hit that attack-command.
Mana costs (70-110 Q, 40-20 W, 60 flat E, 100 flat R) plus W's soldier-charge cost can meaningfully cap how many casts fit into the 15s window depending on mana pool/regen.

Q requires an already-active Sand Soldier to dash-stab through the dummy (spear length 325, dash target ~50 units past the cursor), and E requires dashing to the nearest active soldier, passing through the dummy en route; both assume the soldier is positioned so the dash/stab actually connects with the single target.

needsBespoke.why: Azir's damage output is built around a single shared entity - the Sand Soldier - that W creates/stocks, that Q sends dashing (dealing its own damage instance), and that E dashes toward (dealing damage along the way and, on hitting an enemy champion, refunding a W charge). No single primitive in the closed list captures this three-way dependency (a pet that is simultaneously an ammo resource for W, a required target for E, and a projectile launched by Q). Additionally, whether two simultaneously-active soldiers (from holding 2 W charges) can both attack the same dummy on one basic-attack command - doubling the per-attack magic damage instance, with the second reduced by the 25% subsequent-attack modifier - is a stacking pet-attack interaction the primitive list does not model explicitly; it would need bespoke logic to decide how many soldiers are 'active and attacking' at once.

proposal: Open by casting R once (long cooldown, 200-600 base + 0.75 AP) early in the fight so its ~0.5s cast/travel delay does not push it out of the 15s window and it isn't wasted on cooldown.
Cast W to summon a Sand Soldier next to the dummy as soon as possible so subsequent basic attacks route through the soldier's stab.
Basic-attack the dummy continuously; each attack command routes through the active soldier for its magic-damage stab (at 50% on-hit/on-attack effectiveness) instead of Azir's own auto-attack.

Recast W whenever a charge is available (respecting the 1.5s cooldown and mana/soldier-stock cost) to keep a soldier active for the full fight and, if a second simultaneous soldier is possible, to add a second stab instance per attack.
Weave Q on cooldown (14s down to 6s) for its direct magic-damage dash-stab through the dummy, since it requires an already-active soldier which W keeps supplying.

Weave E on cooldown (22s down to 16s) to dash through the dummy for its own magic damage instance, and, if dashing into an enemy champion grants a bonus Arise! charge, cast it as soon as a soldier exists to help refresh W's stock.
Continue this Q/E/basic-attack loop for the remainder of the 15s, always keeping at least one Sand Soldier active via W so basic attacks are never wasted as plain Azir auto-attacks.
questions: At what level and with what item build is this fight simulated, since it changes which W bonus-damage tier and SecondaryTargetDamageMod tier apply, and whether the R cast time even matters relative to the 15s window?

Should R be included in the optimal rotation at all given its very long cooldown (90-120s) means it will only ever be cast once (or not at all) in a single 15s fight - does the simulator want single-cast abilities counted?

Is E's self-shield (defensive, not affecting damage dealt) ever worth casting purely for the damage tick and possible W-charge refund, or should it be skipped if it risks interrupting the attack-command queue (since movement/attack commands are cancelled during the E dash)?

Does the dummy fight's single stationary target let the soldier's line-attack ever hit more than one 'target' (relevant to the SecondaryTargetDamageMod), or is that entirely inert in this fight and only the primary-target damage numbers matter?
